newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks to see corrective sales on US plunge.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks to see corrective sales on US plunge.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to see corrective sales on Tuesday, depressed by the sell off on Wall Street, which was triggered by comments by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto about potential sales of U.S. Treasuries by Japan, brokers said.
On Monday, the 225-share Nikkei average gained 50.60 points, or 0.25 percent, to end at 20,436.14. Its September futures ended down 60 at 20,410.
"We're likely to see a correction in Tokyo, and the Nikkei may fall close to 20,000," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager of the equities operations group at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
Brokers said the Nikkei 225 average, which has been supported by U.S. stocks' extended record rally, could continue to consolidate and fall through 20,000 later this week.
"But investors' firm demand in the telecommunications sector would support stocks at the downside," said a broker at a second-tier Japanese securities house.
In New York on Monday, the Dow industrials fell about 192 points or 2.5 percent to 7,604. It was the second-largest single-day point drop ever.
In Chicago, Nikkei 225 futures closed at 20,220, down 190 points from their close in Osaka on Monday.

Hashimoto said in New York on Monday he would like the United States to cooperate in stabilising foreign exchange rates because currency volatility might cause the Japanese government to sell its holdings of U.S. government securities.

"I hope the U.S. will engage in efforts and in cooperation to maintain exchange stability so we will not succumb to the temptation to sell off Treasury bills and switch our funds to gold," Hashimoto said.

Japan's Ministry of Finance said in a statement that Hashimoto regretted that his intentions had not been accurately conveyed. It said Japan will continue to cooperate with the United States in seeking stability in foreign exchange markets.
First-section turnover on the Tokyo Stock Exchange was 170 million shares, against 157 million at Monday midday. Losers outpaced gainers 745 to 249 and 239 issues were unchanged.
In other indices, the broader-based TOPIX index declined 6.70 points or 0.44 percent to 1,524.22. The Nikkei 300 average fell 1.44 point or 0.49 percent to 294.73.
By sector, losers were led by transport equipment, fisheries, real estate, warehousing and sea transport. The only notable gainers were pulp/paper and banks.
Shares in Sakura Bank Ltd and Shizuoka Bank Ltd climbed on their announcements of share repurchases.
Sakura, a major commercial bank, rose 15 yen to end the morning at 857. Its volume was the heaviest on the first section at 5.146 million shares.
Shizuoka Bank was up 50 yen at 1,300. Volume was 901,000 shares.
Shares in Terumo Corp slipped, hurt by newspaper reports about its intravenous food supplements. Terumo was down 30 yen at 2,130.

Japan Tobacco Inc's shares also fell, as concerns over the domestic tobacco industry grew on news that the U.S. tobacco industry, health advocates and 40 states suing the industry had reached a $368.5 billion landmark settlement. Japan Tobacco's shares fell 27,000 yen to 891,000. -- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
